thread:
emma: heads-up 11 week: our team has 4 on-site interviews scheduled during the company holiday blackout (Dec 24Dec 31). recruiting asked if we can keep them. any guidance for scheduling and PTO implications?

jess (People Ops): quick policy refresher: company-wide shutdown = default no-interview window, but exceptions exist for critical hires. exceptions must be requested by the hiring manager and recruiting and approved by people-ops at least 10 business days before the scheduled interviews. managers need to confirm interviewer availability and whether interviewers will be on PTO.

raj (recruiting): thanks. these are two IC+PM hires that are on tight timelines. candidates are only available those dates. can interviewers be scheduled as "working during blackout" without using PTO?

jess (People Ops): interviewers who work during the company shutdown must be either on an approved duty rotation (so they are considered working) or use PTO for any personal time they would otherwise have taken. we generally give managers flexibility to mark specific people as "essential coverage" for interviewing, but they must document why this is business-critical and propose a coverage/comp time plan.

maria (ENG): to clarify: if I'm asked to take a 3-hour interview slot on Dec 27, do I need to bank comp time or is that a straight work hour?

jess (People Ops): short answer: treated as work hours if the manager designates it as part of the team's essential hiring window and the manager records it in the coverage plan. manager must also coordinate whether the interviewer will get comp time (floating hours) or an alternate day off. please document comp arrangements in the request.

emma: what about accrual/carryover effects for folks who are on the team rotation and therefore formally "worked" part of the shutdown?

jess (People Ops): accruals follow payroll status. if someone is marked working (approved duty rotation) they are considered active and accruals continue normally. if someone was going to be on PTO that week and they volunteer to work interviews instead, they should choose whether to convert that PTO into comp time (manager-approved) or maintain PTO and decline. any comp time given must be scheduled within the next 90 days.

raj (recruiting): what's the approval workflow? I can submit the exception but who signs off?

jess (People Ops): workflow: 1) hiring manager + recruiting draft an exception request with rationale, interviewer names, hours, and proposed comp plan; 2) manager submits to people-ops via the portal -> people-ops reviews and approves/asks questions; 3) if approved, operations will notify payroll/manager and add the duty rotation to the blackout tracker. approvals ideally 10 business days prior.

maria (ENG): we have a senior interviewer who is on parental leave and technically not active. can we call them in to do interviews remotely?

jess (People Ops): staff on active parental leave are not required to work. if they volunteer, they must explicitly opt in and compensation/comp time must be agreed before they do the work. for unpaid LOA cases, please get written consent and schedule the time as paid at the manager's direction; people-ops will advise on payroll coding.

emma: any templates I should use when submitting?

jess (People Ops): yes use this minimal template in the portal submission: 

```
Exception request: Holiday blackout - interviews
Hiring team: <team name>
Roles: <role names>
Candidate windows: <dates/times>
Interviewers: <list>
Rationale: <business-critical reason>
Coverage/comp plan: <who covers, how comp time paid back>
Manager approval: <name/date>
Recruiting contact: <name>
```

people-ops-bot: Reminder: "Holiday blackout exceptions (interviews): submit >=10 business days prior. Include comp plan and interviewer list." <https://hr.redwood.com/blackout-exceptions>

raj (recruiting): i'll put the draft in the portal today and tag you, @jess.

emma: thanks all  will coordinate interviewers and comp scheduling.

jess (People Ops): thanks team. one last note: if an exception is denied, recruiting should reschedule candidates or offer a remote asynchronous interview (take-home exercise + recorded panel) to avoid forcing anyone on PTO.
